scope.description: Whole pandoc application/library breadth across useful functional families.
scope.denominator: Document parsing/writing across formats, structured documents, citations, mathematics, templates/styles, filters and publication metadata.

coverage.rationale: A coherent small-report pipeline spans HTML, DOCX and EPUB with checked author/description declarations, but broad readers, citations, maths, styling and document transformations remain absent. The additional metadata stays within a small publication slice, so the coarse whole-application estimate remains 15%.

scope.description: Structured sections/tables/images and pinned transcript blocks, with ordered author and description declarations, to HTML, DOCX and optional EPUB 3.
scope.denominator: User intent and domain decisions within the named supported workflows, including declared inputs, composition and useful outputs; excluded application features do not enter this score.

abstraction.rationale: Report structure, transcript provenance and consistent publication metadata express intent without markup or writer commands; supported author/description choices remain bounded and style/editorial decisions remain restricted. Abstraction remains 80% within this explicitly expanded report slice.

limitations: Closed bounded report model; no authored markup, templates, filters, bibliography or broad input formats; EPUBCheck is a separate workflow, not implicit certification. Authors and descriptions are declarations, not verified identity or review; fixed native reader behaviour is version-bound.

Subjective review of current source contracts and bounded evidence, not an exhaustive native API measurement. Native results cover named cases; source-bound qualification and runtime availability must be queried separately.
